# architecture.md ## Project Architecture Overview **hevy-mcp** is a [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) server for the [Hevy](https://www.hevyapp.com/) fitness API. It lets AI assistants read, analyze, create, and update workouts, routines, exercise templates, and body measurements through authenticated Hevy API requests [[1]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/86385d8b-fd28-42af-bebd-e017cd533d92). The codebase is a TypeScript monorepo organized as a **private workspace orchestrator** with six packages under `packages/`. The root has no runtime `src/` tree — all implementation lives in the workspaces [[2]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/947ebc0f-60be-4a4e-b227-238f01cd75a6). The defining architectural property is that a **single MCP tool contract runs identically on two very different runtimes**: ```text Hosted: AI assistant → Streamable HTTP → Cloudflare Worker → Hevy API Local: AI assistant → MCP over stdio → local hevy-mcp → Hevy API ``` [[3]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/86385d8b-fd28-42af-bebd-e017cd533d92) This is achieved by keeping the tool implementations and API client runtime-neutral, then composing them into runtime-specific adapters (Node.js and Cloudflare Workers) that never share code with each other [[4]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae). The six workspaces and their roles at a glance: | Workspace | Package name | Role | | ---------------------- | ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | | `packages/hevy-client` | `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client` | Runtime-neutral API client (Kubb-generated) | | `packages/operations` | `@hevy-mcp/operations` | Runtime-neutral shared operations layer | | `packages/core` | `@hevy-mcp/core` | Runtime-neutral MCP tools and server construction | | `packages/node` | `hevy-mcp` | Node.js stdio/HTTP adapter — the only publishable workspace | | `packages/worker` | `@hevy-mcp/worker` | Private Cloudflare Worker HTTP/OAuth adapter | | `packages/cli` | `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli` | Public Hevy command-line client | [[5]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/947ebc0f-60be-4a4e-b227-238f01cd75a6) ## Workspace Dependency Diagram The shipped composition graph flows from the runtime-neutral packages outward to the platform adapters and public CLI [[6]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae): ```mermaid graph TD HC["@hevy-mcp/hevy-client
runtime-neutral API client"] OPS["@hevy-mcp/operations
runtime-neutral operations layer"] CORE["@hevy-mcp/core
runtime-neutral MCP tools & server"] NODE["hevy-mcp
Node.js stdio/HTTP adapter"] WORKER["@hevy-mcp/worker
Cloudflare Worker HTTP/OAuth adapter"] CLI["@chrisdoc/hevy-cli
public CLI"] HC --> OPS HC --> CORE OPS --> CORE CORE --> NODE CORE --> WORKER CORE --> CLI style HC fill:#d4edda,stroke:#28a745 style OPS fill:#d4edda,stroke:#28a745 style CORE fill:#d4edda,stroke:#28a745 style NODE fill:#cce5ff,stroke:#004085 style WORKER fill:#fff3cd,stroke:#856404 style CLI fill:#cce5ff,stroke:#004085 ``` **Legend:** Green = runtime-neutral · Blue = Node.js adapter · Amber = Cloudflare adapter Key constraints to observe in this diagram [[7]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/947ebc0f-60be-4a4e-b227-238f01cd75a6): - `hevy-client`, `operations`, and `core` are **runtime-neutral**: they contain no Node.js built-ins and no Cloudflare-specific bindings, making them safe to import and execute in either runtime. - `hevy-mcp` (Node) and `@hevy-mcp/worker` (Cloudflare) both consume `core` but **must never import each other**. This boundary is enforced by the `package-boundaries` validation lane [[8]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/c4ac07dbe84a7e83ba88a5073f0a83ab34af5c86/repository/validation-lanes.json#L209-L227). - `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli` bundles the runtime-neutral packages directly and does **not** depend on either adapter. - `@hevy-mcp/core` depends on both `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client` and `@hevy-mcp/operations` [[9]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/packages/core/package.json#L20-L24); `@hevy-mcp/operations` depends on `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client` [[10]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/47eac6bd864bbfc1d66bbd48881df895e1a4214e/packages/operations/package.json#L16-L18). > [!IMPORTANT] > The adapter packages (`hevy-mcp` and `@hevy-mcp/worker`) must never import one another. Violating this constraint would pull Node-specific or Cloudflare-specific code into the wrong runtime bundle and cause hard failures at runtime. ## Runtime-Neutral vs. Platform Adapters ### What "runtime-neutral" means A package is **runtime-neutral** when it makes no assumptions about the JavaScript host environment. Concretely, this means: - **No Node.js built-ins**: `process`, `fs`, `child_process`, `path`, `crypto` (Node's version), etc. are forbidden. - **No Cloudflare-specific bindings**: KV namespaces, Durable Objects, environment secrets injected via `env` object, and Worker-specific globals are forbidden. ## 1. Exercise template catalog / `AsyncTtlCache` lifetime

**Construction:** `createExerciseTemplateCatalog` (`packages/core/src/utils/exercise-template-catalog.ts:33-90`) allocates a **private** `AsyncTtlCache` (TTL 5 min, `maxSize: 1`, key `"exercise-template-catalog"`). Not a process-wide singleton.

**Who constructs it:** only `createHevyMcpServer` (`packages/core/src/server.ts:60-70`):

```ts
catalog: createExerciseTemplateCatalog(client, options.cacheObserver)
```

Adapters call that factory; they do not own the cache.

| Adapter | Lifetime |
|---|---|
| Node executable | **One catalog per process/server.** `packages/node/src/runtime.ts:211-226` `buildServer()` → one `createHevyMcpServer`. Same for embed API `packages/node/src/index.ts:29-36`. |
| Worker | **Per MCP request.** `packages/worker/src/worker.ts:305-317` + `421-428`: `createDefaultServer` / `createServer` runs inside `serveMcpRequest`. Isolate-wide schema preload exists; catalog does not. |

**Sharing today:** `createToolRuntime` (`packages/core/src/tools/tool-runtime.ts:209-220`) keeps the **same catalog object**. `forExecution` wraps `get()` with request `execution` but `reset()` still hits the shared cache. Effect layer is **request-local** (`packages/core/src/effect-layer.ts:30-45`) and only `Layer.succeed(ExerciseTemplateCatalogService, catalog)` — it does not create a new cache.

**Would request-local Effect Cache break cross-call caching?** **Yes**, if the Cache is created inside `createCoreServiceLayer` / per-execution `ToolRuntime`. Node stdio/HTTP would lose TTL hits across tool calls. Worker already has no cross-request catalog anyway.

**Where Effect Cache should live:** construct **once next to the catalog**, in `createHevyMcpServer` (server/session scope), then provide that instance via `Layer.succeed` the same way catalog is provided. Do not instantiate Cache in a per-request Layer. Optional later: Worker isolate-scoped cache keyed by API key (not in topology today).

---

## 2. Package topology

Source: `repository/topology.json`. Enforcement: `scripts/check-package-boundaries.mjs` + `tests/unit/package-boundaries.test.ts`. Depcruise is a spike only (`docs/nx-dependency-cruiser-spike.md`).

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Can **operations** import `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client/internal`? | **Yes.** `allowed: { "@hevy-mcp/hevy-client": ["", "types", "internal"] }`. Used in `packages/operations/src/index.ts`. |
| Can **core** import `hevy-client/internal`? | **No.** core allowed: `["", "types", "schemas"]` only. |
| Can **core** depend on operations? | **Yes.** dependency + `allowed: { "@hevy-mcp/operations": [""] }`. |
| Can **CLI** depend on operations? | **Yes.** topology + `allowed: { "@hevy-mcp/operations": [""] }`. |
| Can **node/worker** depend on operations **directly**? | **No.** Both allowed only `@hevy-mcp/core` `""` and `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client` `""`. `packages/node/package.json` / `packages/worker/package.json` do not list operations. They must go through core. |

**Export-map / Effect-returning ops:** operations public API is a **single** `"."` export (`packages/operations/package.json`, topology `"exports": ["."]`). Changing `execute` to return `Effect` is allowed on that surface; no extra subpath is required. Do **not** leak `/internal` through core. Consumers of `"."` are core + CLI (release bundle: operations → core, cli). Node/worker stay Promise-shaped unless core collapses Effects.

---

## 3. CLI command surface vs operations

File: `packages/cli/src/commands/index.ts`. Default: `createOperations(client)` in `execute()`.

**Already on operations:**
- `workouts list` (`executeWorkoutList`)
- `routines list` (`executeRoutineList`)

**Still on `HevyClient` (switch candidates):**
- `user` → `getUserInfo`
- `workouts get|create|update|count|events`
- `routines get|create|update`
- `exercises create|get|history|search` (`search` paginates `getExerciseTemplates`)
- `measurements list|get|create|update`
- `folders create`
- `summary` (paged `getWorkouts` + local aggregation)

Ops today only implement `workouts.get/list` and `routines.get/list` (`packages/operations/src/index.ts`). CLI `get` still uses the client even though ops already have get.

---

## 4. `effect-collapse.test.ts` invariant

File: `packages/operations/src/effect-collapse.test.ts`.

`assertCollapsedExecute(operation.execute.toString())` requires:
1. **exactly one** `Effect.runPromise`
2. **no** `Effect.tryPromise` / `Effect.promise`
3. **contains** `Effect.catchIf`

Live shape (`packages/operations/src/workouts.ts:115-142`): seam returns Effect; `execute` maps/catches then `return Effect.runPromise(program)` → **Promise**.

If ops `execute` returned Effect and **handlers** called `runPromise`:
- `execute.toString()` would have **0** `runPromise` → tests fail.
- Last test `await operation.execute(...)` would hang on an unrun Effect (or resolve to the Effect object).
- Double `runPromise` (ops + handler) would violate “one Effect boundary.”

Handlers would need to become the **only** `runPromise`; the collapse test would need to inspect the handler/program, not `execute.toString()`.

---

## 5. Staged changeset (not modified)

`.changeset/amber-rivers-heal.md` — **minor** on all six packages:

> feat: adopt Effect v4 request-local retry schedules in the Hevy client retry path. Client retries interpreted through Effect with request-local schedule locality; fetch config merge characterization tests; pure read error classification centralized. One Effect runtime boundary; no parallel policy logic.

This is the **client retry / Effect interpreter** cascade, not catalog/cache work.
